lines.say: After a hurricane, officials check if Waffle House is open.
Florida, 2004. Four fucking hurricanes in one season.
The phones were dead, the power was out, and nobody could say how bad it was.
Craig Fugate ran Florida's emergency management. He needed one thing that never closes.
A Waffle House. Open twenty-four hours, every damn day, even in a hurricane.
Full menu means green, the town's holding up. Closed means red, and that's where you send help first.
In 2011, a tornado hit Joplin, Missouri. Two point eight billion dollars of damage.
Both Waffle Houses stayed open. That told them the town could bounce back.
Your clients work the same way. When a regular stops showing up, that's a Waffle House going dark.
Message Health watches your regulars, and texts the ones who go dark before they're gone for good.
